title: 讲座例证目的题
goal: 找到实例所说明的观点；判断实例在论述中的作用。

points.label: 找到实例所说明的观点
判断实例在论述中的作用

sources.title: 大学英语六级（CET-6）：课表
sources.used: 讲座的教学内容、知识点与练习规格

body.p: 例证目的题问讲者为什么提到某个实例。正确选项说的是实例和观点的关系，不是实例本身的内容。观点可能在实例之前，也可能在实例之后。

body.box: A shared shelf can serve several purposes. For example, neighbors may leave books there for others to borrow.

body.p: 书籍借阅是共享书架用途的实例。实例的作用是说明书架的一种用途，不是介绍某一本书。

steps.d: 题干通常点出讲者提及的对象。关于 books 的提问指向共享书架的借阅实例。
听实例前后的概括句。several purposes 是书籍借阅所对应的观点。
判断实例是说明、支持、对比还是例外。书籍借阅展示了书架的一种用途。
正确选项说出实例在论述中的作用。只复述 neighbors leave books 的选项不对。

cards.title: 概念与判断
rows: 说明概念
A returnable container can be used again. A glass bottle is collected and refilled.
瓶子展示容器重复使用的含义。
说明概念
A queue is an ordered line. Passengers wait in the order they arrive.
乘客等候展示排队次序。
支持判断
A change in layout can affect access. After a ramp was added, more visitors entered independently.
独立进门的访客增多，支持布局影响通行的判断。
支持判断
A reminder can improve attendance. More members came after a message was sent.
出席人数的变化支持提醒的作用。
cards.note: 实例要对应原文中具体的那个观点。一项观察只在所述条件下支持这个判断。

cards.title: 对比与例外
rows: 形成对比
Paper can be folded; a rigid board retains its shape.
硬板与纸张的弯曲能力不同。
形成对比
One route is direct, while another passes several stops.
两条路线在经过的地点上不同。
指出例外
Most seeds were dry; one packet had become damp.
潮湿的种子包不符合多数情况。
指出例外
Most rooms were quiet; the room beside the lift was noisy.
电梯旁的房间偏离多数房间的情况。
cards.note: 对比要保留比较的双方。例外只涉及所说的那个对象。

body.box: A storage system can make objects easier to locate without increasing the amount of space. In one workshop, workers labeled the existing drawers by tool type. They then found the tools they needed more quickly, even though no drawers had been added.

Why does the speaker mention the labeled drawers?
1. To describe a workshop that added more storage space
2. To illustrate a way of improving access without extra space
3. To contrast tool labels with a list of workers' names
4. To show that every workshop uses the same tool type

body.p: make objects easier to locate without increasing the amount of space 是实例前的观点。抽屉标签展示了这一关系，即第二项。

cards.title: 干扰项
rows: 只复述内容
Workers labeled existing drawers.
此句未说明实例与观点的关系。
改变关系
The workshop added more drawers.
原文说 no drawers had been added。
错误对比
Labels are compared with workers' names.
原文比较的是查找与空间。
扩大范围
Every workshop uses the same tools.
实例只涉及一个车间。

lines.text: A reusable package can serve the same purpose more than once. A jar that is returned, cleaned, and filled again is one example. The jar need not be replaced after its first use.

items.stem: What idea does the jar illustrate?
options: A package can be used repeatedly for its purpose.
Every jar is filled only once before disposal.
A returned jar is cleaned but not filled again.
A jar is replaced whenever its contents are removed.
items.why: serve the same purpose more than once 是玻璃罐所说明的概念，即第一项。

lines.text: Changing the placement of a sign may affect whether visitors notice it. In one building, a sign beside the entrance was noticed by more visitors than the same sign beside the stairs.

items.stem: Why does the speaker mention the sign beside the entrance?
options: To describe the sign placed beside the stairs
To support a claim about the effect of placement
To show that visitors notice every sign equally
To contrast two different signs in one building
items.why: was noticed by more visitors 支持前句关于标志位置影响注意的判断，即第二项。

lines.text: A fixed shelf stays in one position. A movable shelf, by contrast, can be shifted to make room for another activity.

items.stem: Why is the movable shelf mentioned?
options: To show that a fixed shelf makes room for activities
To describe the one position a fixed shelf keeps
To contrast two ways shelves can be positioned
To show that both kinds of shelf can be moved
items.why: by contrast 将 can be shifted 与 stays in one position 对比，即第三项。

lines.text: Most of the library's study rooms have windows. One interior room, however, has no window. It is used for the same kind of quiet study.

items.stem: What general observation does the interior room qualify?
options: Every study room is used for quiet study.
Rooms without windows are not used for study.
Most of the study rooms are interior rooms.
Most study rooms in the library have windows.
items.why: Most of the library's study rooms have windows 是被无窗房间限定的概括，即第四项。

lines.text: A temporary display can help staff learn how people move through a room. At a fictional museum, staff placed a table near one doorway for a week and observed where visitors walked. They found that the table left a narrow passage beside the door. Most visitors took the wider route around the other side. One visitor using a small cart, however, was able to pass through the narrow space. That exception did not change the general observation that most visitors used the wider route.

items.stem: What point does the table example help explain?
options: A temporary arrangement can reveal movement through a room.
Every museum visitor prefers to walk beside a doorway.
A narrow passage cannot be used by any visitor.
A visitor with a cart requires the widest possible route.
items.why: help staff learn how people move through a room 是桌子实例说明的观点，即第一项。

items.stem: Why does the speaker mention the visitor with a cart?
options: To establish that all visitors chose the narrow route
To identify an exception to the more common route
To show that carts need the wider route
To explain why most visitors chose the wider route
items.why: One visitor using a small cart 与 most visitors took the wider route 构成例外，即第二项。

lines.text: Today we'll consider how a public collection can be arranged to support different kinds of use. A collection is not simply a set of objects; the way those objects are grouped can help people make connections among them. Let me begin with the idea of a thematic arrangement. By this I mean placing objects together because they share a subject, even if they were made at different times. Imagine a display in which an old hand pump stands beside a modern tap. Both relate to access to water, although they belong to different periods. The pair illustrates what a shared subject can contribute to an arrangement. Visitors can compare the objects' functions without first following a complete history of either object. A chronological arrangement follows a different principle. In a second imagined display, the same pump is placed among objects made before the tap. Visitors move from earlier objects to later ones. This contrast shows that the order of a display can express either a subject relationship or a sequence in time. The objects themselves need not change when the organizing principle changes. Neither arrangement answers every question. A thematic group can bring together objects that look different, but it may leave visitors uncertain about when each was made. Dates on labels can supply that information without turning the whole display into a timeline. A chronological display can make a sequence visible, but visitors may need additional explanation to connect objects that appear far apart. Consider a fictional library that grouped maps from different periods by the routes they depicted. Readers could compare how the same journey was represented. Staff reported that visitors asked more questions about the routes after the maps were grouped this way. That observation supports the idea that grouping by subject can direct attention toward a shared issue, although it describes only that library. There can also be exceptions within a planned arrangement. Most of the library's maps were displayed by route, but one fragile map remained in a separate case because it needed different protection. Its position did not represent a different route. It reflected a conservation requirement. An arrangement therefore expresses a choice about relationships, and practical conditions can qualify how completely the choice is applied.

items.stem: What idea is illustrated by placing the pump beside the tap?
options: A display should follow the history of each object.
Objects should be shown in the order they were made.
Visitors must learn each object's date before comparing.
Objects may be grouped by subject across different periods.
items.why: placing objects together because they share a subject, even if they were made at different times 是水泵与水龙头实例说明的概念，即第四项。

items.stem: Why does the speaker describe a display ordered from earlier to later objects?
options: To show that the pump was made before the tap
To explain why a fragile map needs a separate case
To contrast order in time with grouping by subject
To explain how dates on labels can help visitors
items.why: A chronological arrangement follows a different principle 与前面的 thematic arrangement 对比，即第三项。

items.stem: Why is the fragile map mentioned?
options: To show that every map was grouped by its date
To identify an exception caused by a conservation need
To show that a fragile map depicted a different route
To support the claim that grouping maps raised questions
items.why: Most of the library's maps were displayed by route, but one fragile map remained in a separate case 表明这是保护需要造成的例外，即第二项。

lines.text: This talk concerns the way a service can be tested before a permanent change is made. A trial is a limited attempt to learn about a proposal under specified conditions. For example, a community center might offer a borrowed equipment service on two afternoons before deciding whether to extend it. The two afternoons are not a complete service history. They provide an opportunity to observe the proposed arrangement on a small scale. To interpret a trial, the observations must be connected to the question being asked. Imagine that the center wants to know whether a desk near the entrance helps visitors find the borrowing service. During one trial afternoon, staff place the desk near the entrance. During another, they place it inside the main room. The same signs and equipment are used on both occasions. In this fictional comparison, more visitors ask about borrowing when the desk is near the entrance. The example supports the idea that position can influence whether a service is noticed. It does not establish why every visitor made a particular choice. Notice that the comparison concerns the location of the desk. It does not compare the quality of the equipment, because the equipment is unchanged. Nor does it tell us whether the people who asked questions would later borrow anything. Asking and borrowing are different actions. A second distinction concerns an observation and an explanation. The staff can count the questions people ask. They might suggest that the desk was easier to see near the entrance, but the count alone does not show where visitors looked. Both statements can be useful if their different roles are kept clear. Trials also have practical limitations. Most visitors during the two afternoons arrived on foot, but one arrived with a large wheeled case. This exception reminds staff that a route comfortable for many visitors may be harder for someone carrying a bulky object. Staff could observe the doorway and ask visitors about access during a later trial. They could also repeat the comparison at different times of day. The main point is that a trial provides evidence about a particular arrangement under particular conditions. Its value lies in connecting the observation to the original question while retaining details that might matter when the service changes.

items.stem: What idea is illustrated by offering the service on two afternoons?
options: A trial is a limited attempt to examine a proposal.
A permanent service requires exactly two afternoons.
Two afternoons give a complete service history.
A permanent change should be made before testing.
items.why: A trial is a limited attempt to learn about a proposal 是两次下午服务说明的定义，即第一项。

items.stem: What claim does the desk comparison support?
options: Equipment quality changes whenever a desk is moved.
Every visitor who asks a question later borrows equipment.
A service's location can affect whether it is noticed.
Visitors always look at the entrance before the main room.
items.why: more visitors ask about borrowing when the desk is near the entrance 支持 position can influence whether a service is noticed，即第三项。

items.stem: Why does the speaker distinguish counting questions from suggesting an explanation?
options: To show that asking and borrowing are two separate actions
To compare a recorded observation with an interpretation
To prove that all visitors looked directly at the desk
To illustrate why the signs differed between afternoons
items.why: count the questions 是观察，suggest that the desk was easier to see 是解释，第二项保留了二者区别。
